get.summary: Public keys for verifying access tokens
get.description:
The public half of the signing key, as a JWK Set.

Public by design: anyone may verify a token, only this service may mint one.
Cached for five minutes so payments does not refetch on every request, but
not so long that a key rotation takes hours to propagate.

post.description:
Register a TASK_SUBMITTER.

The response is built from an explicit schema rather than dumping the
model, so the password hash cannot leak by accident.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for an access token and a refresh cookie
post.description: Authenticate, mint a 15 minute access token, and set the refresh cookie.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh cookie for a new access token
post.description:
Single-use rotation.

The presented token is revoked and replaced. Presenting an already-revoked
token destroys every session for that user: two parties holding one cookie
means one of them stole it, and there is no way to tell which.

Reuse is caught here rather than left to the global handler. The service
revokes the chain in this request's transaction, and an exception escaping
the route would roll that back, throwing away the revocation at exactly the
moment it matters. Returning the 401 lets the request finish and commit.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or already-used token

post.summary: Revoke the refresh token and clear the cookie
post.description:
Idempotent.

Logging out is a request to end a session; a client that already lost its
cookie has achieved that, so an unknown token is not an error.

Returns nothing so FastAPI keeps the injected response, which is what
carries the cookie-clearing header.

get.description:
Read from the database, not from the token.

The role is whatever the row says now, so a demotion applies immediately
rather than when the access token happens to expire.

get.summary: Is there a cached flow for this task?
get.description: The task signature and, if one is stored, the flow's statistics. `eligible` is whether an ordinary run would replay it: a flow below the configured success rate is kept and not used, until three runs have passed judgement on it and it is deleted.

post.summary: Run a finished task's flow again
post.description: Creates a new task bound to the cached flow of this one, and queues it. The replay is unconditional: the success rate that gates ordinary runs is not consulted, because the user has asked for this sequence. The original task is untouched, since it is the record of what happened. Replay stops at the first step that does not verify and the planner carries on from there, so the new task completes on its own terms either way.

ApprovalDecisionRequest.title: ApprovalDecisionRequest
ApprovalDecisionRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /tasks/{id}/approve`` and ``/reject``.

``approved`` is in the body because spec section 6 puts it there, and the
endpoint decides the outcome. The two must agree: the route checks it, so
``{"approved": false}`` sent to ``/approve`` is a 400 rather than an
approval. A client that disagrees with itself about something irreversible
is a client to stop, not one to guess at.

ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus
ApprovalStatus.description:
Spec section 5, approvals.approval_status.

``EXPIRED`` drives the task to ``TIMED_OUT`` per decision A4; ``REJECTED``
is reserved for an explicit human rejection.
